correctness.rationale: For all N>=6 congruent 2 mod 4, the gauge is the maximum of N apothem-normalized supporting functionals. Dihedral symmetry and Sain–Ghosh–Paul vertex reduction reduce the James maximum to v=(1,0) and its unique isosceles unit partner (0,cos(pi/N)). The angular inequality pi/4-pi/(2N)<atan(cos(pi/N))<pi/4 selects normal pi/4+pi/(2N) for N=2 mod8 and pi/4-pi/(2N) for N=6 mod8; direct trigonometric identities produce both signs, and Taylor expansion gives the third-order residue term. Independent direct facet-max numerical checks for ten orders N=6..98 matched to 2e-14; the infinite claim follows from the geometric argument, not numerical samples.
